prompt: Solve for $x$: $5(x - 1) - 2x = 2x + 7$. Give just the number.
hint: Do the full cleanup routine: distribute the $5$, then combine like terms on the left.

hints.text: Do the full cleanup routine: distribute the $5$, then combine like terms on the left.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up by distributing only: $5(x - 1)$ is $5x - 5$. Now the left side is $5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$. Much friendlier!
$5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$, so the equation is $3x - 5 = 2x + 7$. Subtract $2x$ from both sides.

explanation: Combine like terms on the left: $5x - 5 - 2x = 3x - 5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tidy each room first
steps: Treat each side like a messy room: you cannot compare them until both are tidy.
Left room tidied: $3x - 5$. Right room is already tidy: $2x + 7$.
Now the equation $3x - 5 = 2x + 7$ is a simple both-sides problem: $x = 12$.
